finding.expected: Make predecessor-bearing lineage accept one unambiguous canonical four-field shape (`source_run_id`, `review_id`, `finding_id`, `reviewed_sha`) and reject extra/alias or conflicting identity representations rather than choosing one. Validate source RUN identity consistently with the repository's existing canonical RUN namespace so the Operator and publication boundaries cannot disagree. Add focused regressions proving conflicting/alternate predecessor fields fail closed and a canonically admissible RUN identity is interpreted consistently, while preserving the legacy no-predecessor path.
finding.issue: The new predecessor identity parser is not a single fail-closed canonical grammar. Both Operator and publication accept alias keys (`run_id`, `source_review_id`, `selected_finding_id`) in addition to the four Runtime-persisted canonical keys and resolve them with `canonical_value or alias_value`. A malformed predecessor record can therefore contain both forms with conflicting identities and still be accepted because one value silently wins instead of the inconsistency failing closed. In addition, Operator validates `source_run_id` with a new private regex that is narrower than the existing canonical RUN/ref grammar used by publication and `task_run_prefix`, so the same predecessor identity can be accepted by one boundary and rejected by the other. This violates AC3's exact inconsistent-identity fail-closed requirement and undermines one reproducible predecessor contract.
